data.name: Rhule
data.headline: A nice and comfortable stay in Lisbon
data.pros:
We loved the very kind Check-in, we got to know about the happy hour, received discount vouchers for the restaurant. In general the staff was very kind and friendly. 
The room had everything needed, wad clean and even the cleaning service was so quick and attentive. 
We also enjoyed the location very much of the Hotel, als you can walk to the City center easily by foot.
data.cons:
Unfortunately the food was not fitting to the quality that would fit to this kind of good hotel.
The breakfast had a great variety of items but the quality wasn’t quiet nice. Many items came out of cans (mushrooms, pineapple, etc.), the coffee was no coffee but some in water dissolved flavor-liquid (here you could easily improve with already exchanging it with filter Coffee since thats actually coffee). And the rest like cheese, meatcuts or sausage just didn’t look appealing thats why we didn’t even try. 
The muesli station was nice, with many milk options. Also the Juices were good.

I would definitely love to come back. Highly recommended!

Relaxation and Convenience Unwind at the hotel's SPA (16+), fitness centre, or library, and take advantage of the meeting facilities for any business needs. data.name: Taiu
data.headline: Fantastic central location within easy walking distance of São Bento Station
data.pros:
The location is incredibly convenient. It is only a couple of minutes' walk from São Bento Station, making it very easy to get to when arriving in the city. You are also within easy walking distance of major landmarks like the Porto Cathedral, Igreja de Santo Ildefonso, the Imperial McDonald's, and the famous Luís I Bridge.

For food and beverages, the hotel is perfectly positioned. It is not far away from Conga (around 5 mins walk), the famous local spot known for its amazing bifana and francesinha. It is also close to Pingo Doce, a handy supermarket located right up the hill near Santa Catarina Street, which is great for grabbing daily essentials...and also boozes.
data.cons: While the hotel is very close to the train station, Porto's streets can be quite steep and uneven. If you are walking with heavy luggage, that short couple-of-minutes walk can definitely feel a bit longer.

data.name: Darunzo
data.pros: The view of the river from the room.
data.cons:
For a hotel that presents itself as one of Porto’s finest five-star luxury hotels, the overall experience fell far short of expectations, especially considering the extremely high price.

Food and Room Service: A Major Disappointment

One of the biggest disappointments was the food. For the price you pay to stay at The Yeatman, you would expect high-quality food that reflects the hotel’s luxury status. Instead, much of what was offered was mediocre, basic food, such as tuna sandwiches and other items that you could easily get from an ordinary takeaway.

The breakfast room service was particularly disappointing. I ordered waffles expecting freshly prepared food, ideally made by a chef. Instead, I received prepackaged, shelf-stable waffles of the kind you can buy in a grocery store. To make matters worse, the hotel charged an additional €10 surcharge just to deliver this basic, non-fresh food to the room.

My partner and I ended up having to go out and find our own food every day. This should not be necessary when staying at a hotel of this price and reputation. A luxury hotel should offer a dining experience that justifies the cost, not food that feels like something you would buy off a supermarket shelf.

Poor Maintenance and an Unacceptable Lighting Issue

The final night of our stay was especially frustrating. The lights in our room stopped working, so I called reception that evening. I was told that the issue would be fixed, but nobody came, leaving us to pack our luggage in the dark.

The following morning, I contacted reception again, only for a different staff member to say they had not heard about the problem. The lights were finally fixed approximately ten minutes before we checked out at 7 a.m. Since it was still dark outside, there was no natural light coming through the windows, and we had to get ready and finish packing in the dark.

For a hotel charging luxury prices, this level of communication and service is unacceptable.

data.name: Melody
data.headline: More like a 4* with very rude staff
data.pros:
Positives: clean, modern, well furnished, comfortable, lovely (small) pool areas both inside and outdoor at the top of the hotel with lovely views, toiletries, robe, slippers, hairdryer, water, fridge and kettle in room
Location: 1 hour walk to Porto, local area has everything you need to eat, drink and shop. Building site right next to hotel which our room looked out on
Negatives: staff were not friendly or helpful and quite rude. More hooks needed in the bathroom and glass doors do not offer privacy. Breakfast was basic. Bar and restaurant overpriced. More loungers needed at both pools, bean bags were not pleasant at the outdoor pool.
Why this isn’t a 5*: Breakfast: you have to pay extra for things which are usually included at buffet breakfasts and what was there was minimal. No balcony. No coffee machine in the bedroom, awful instant sachets. Mini bar contents were not included, they were no extras to make this a 5* experience.

data.name: Erin
data.pros:
Not a great location for getting around as taxis take a really long time to arrive there. 

Definitely would not consider this a 5 star hotel by any means.maybe 3 at best. For the price, i wouldn't say its worth it.

The breakfast was OK. Small, but enough. The staff was mostly good, just very slow at everything they do. The room and beds were good and comfortable. The area is a bit sketchy due to a large migrant population being constantly on the street doing nothing. However, it is within walking distance to the shore, shopping, etc. Overall, nice and would stay there again.

data.name: Alcina Sofia
data.headline: Ótima Localização e excelentes instalações! Recomendo!!
data.pros:
A localização é óptima, mesmo junto à marina e às Ramblas e todos os pontos de interesse de visita na cidade. 
O quarto era muito espaçoso, confortável, e a casa de banho muito funcional e espaçosa também. O pequeno almoço óptimo, com muitas opções de escolha. Os funcionários são muito simpáticos. Tem uma saída/entrada de metro a 150m do hotel. Bastante bom quanto à qualidade/localização/preço e muito sossegado. Limpeza excelente.
Recomendo!
data.cons: Nada a apontar. O meu quarto era óptimo e com tudo o que estava descrito no booking, inclusive as fotografias apresentadas.

data.name: Fernando B.
data.headline: Hotel próximo ao metrô com bom serviço e quarto confortável.
data.pros: O hotel integra a rede Meliá e, como esperávamos, oferece um padrão de serviço e acomodação bastante qualificado. A equipe é gentil e solícita. O quarto tem espaço suficiente para um casal com bagagens grandes. A reposição do frigobar diária e a cortesia de águas, sucos e refrigerante foram muito bem-vindas. O chuveiro era ótimo com fluxo de água suficiente e espaço razoável para utilização com conforto.
data.cons: O café da manhã foi bom, mas durante o período que estivemos hospedados ocorreu de modo bastante repetitivo. Os bolos e doces eram escassos em opções e pouco atraentes. O grande trunfo era a possibilidade de solicitar omeletes ou ovos mexidos diretamente na hora e poder comê-los quentinhos. Existe uma área destinada a alimentos sem glúten, porém com restritas opções, tornando a escolha um processo repetitivo e sem muita evolução ao longo do período de hospedagem. Acredito que neste quesito (café da manhã) é possível melhorar consideravelmente com oferta de mais e melhores opções tanto para público em geral como para aqueles com restrições alimentares.

data.name: Michał
data.headline: Fantastyczne 4 dni w Barcelonie
data.pros: Bardzo dobre śniadania. Duży wybór. Omlety przygotowywane na bieżąco - przepyszne. Kilka ekspresow do kawy zapewniało brak kolejek po kawę.  Hotel nowoczesny,  w fajnym miejscu z racji bliskości metra. ok. 100m. Pokój czysty, z uzupełnianym (napoje) minibarem w cenie.
data.cons: Niestety pokój nie był wystarczajaco wyciszony. Nieszczelne okna, hałas mocno dobiegał z ulicy. Spędziliśmy 4 noce, niestety jednego dnia pominięto sprzątanie pokoju.

data.cons: Da ausência de limpeza do chão do quarto.

data.name: Tara
data.headline: Not worth the Money
data.pros: The breakfast was good but the first day I didn't know there was an a la cart option, so I paid 44 euro for the buffet and only had coffee, yogurt and croissant.   Of course the cocktail and wine prices were quite high so we often ended up going to a neighborhood bistro for such.  Lots of good restaurants in the area, and being close to the Louvre and Musee Orsay was a plus.
data.cons:
I was bitten by bugs (fleas? Bed bugs?) and have the photos to prove it.  They provided a bed ck, said there were no bugs but changed the sheets anyway.  Something was biting me each night.  I booked through Booking.com and will be appealing to them for some kind of compensation.  I have never experienced this in any of the U.S. Hyatt hotels.
Also the traffic noise from our room was disruptive to sleep.  We looked out on the back of the Louvre. Perhaps if we had had a room overlooking the center courtyard it would have been quieter.

data.headline: Dream day in a dream city! Loved it! ￼
data.pros: A dream stay in a dream city! It was comfortable, everyone was very friendly, the location was exceptional, the rooms were comfortable the quiet.
data.cons: Nothing

data.name: Giacomo
data.pros:
Abbiamo apprezzato moltissimo il soggiorno all’Hôtel Duquesne Eiffel, soprattutto per la posizione davvero privilegiata. L’hotel si trova praticamente accanto a Les Invalides e a breve distanza dalla Torre Eiffel, che si raggiunge facilmente con una piacevole passeggiata, attraversando una delle zone più belle di Parigi.
Il quartiere è elegante, curato e ben servito, con numerosi ristoranti, bistrot e attività nelle immediate vicinanze. Nonostante la posizione centrale, conserva un’atmosfera tranquilla e autenticamente parigina, lontana dal turismo più caotico e dalla movida. Una caratteristica che abbiamo particolarmente apprezzato e che lo rende ideale per chi desidera vivere Parigi con ritmi più rilassati.
Abbiamo trovato l’ambiente accogliente e caratteristico, perfettamente in sintonia con il fascino della città. Anche il personale si è dimostrato gentile e disponibile, contribuendo a rendere il soggiorno ancora più piacevole.
Una struttura che consigliamo assolutamente.

data.name: Josef
data.headline: Unser Fazit: Wir hätten dieses Hotel unter diesen Umständen niemals gebucht, wenn wir vorher über die tatsächliche Situa
data.pros: Verständnis von dem Personal.
data.cons:
Enttäuschender und erschreckender Aufenthalt – mangelnde Information über erhebliche Sicherheitsrisiken

Wir sind äußerst enttäuscht von unserem Aufenthalt im Crowne Plaza Paris – République.

Das Hotel liegt direkt am Place de la République und damit mitten im Epizentrum der Demonstrationen und gewalttätigen Ausschreitungen.

Was wir absolut nicht nachvollziehen können: Uns wurde die Buchung ermöglicht, ohne uns auf diese außergewöhnliche Situation und die damit verbundenen Sicherheitsrisiken hinzuweisen.

Während unseres Aufenthalts wurden wir sogar von Demonstranten angegriffen. Unsere Anreise am Samstag dauerte aufgrund der Ausschreitungen und Straßensperrungen unglaubliche sieben Stunden, bis wir endlich das Hotel erreichen konnten.

Das war keine gewöhnliche Unannehmlichkeit, sondern eine Situation, in der wir uns persönlich gefährdet fühlten.

Wir sind der Meinung, dass sowohl das Hotel als auch Booking.com eine Verantwortung gegenüber ihren Gästen haben. Wenn sich ein Hotel inmitten einer solchen Gefahrenlage befindet, erwarten wir eine entsprechende Information und Transparenz gegenüber den Reisenden.

Wir werden deshalb sowohl bei der Hotelgruppe IHG als auch bei Booking.com eine offizielle Beschwerde einreichen und eine angemessene finanzielle Entschädigung verlangen.

We liked the restaurant downstairs and also Neni… we also liked that it was close to the train station.

data.name: stefania
data.pros:
My overall stay was okay, I enjoyed the decor, the vibes, and the restaurant especially, the staff there was very nice, but I must highlight two things. 

The upon arrival the check-in process was a bit slow, and I did not find the personnel too friendly I must admit, perfectly polite and everything but not as enthusiastic or warm as they could have been, I appreciate it is fashion week and it IS busy, but I did notice that. 

Another important and more critical point for me is that the cleanliness of the room could have been definitely better. 

I found a hair in my bed, the room felt dusty and the floors were not super clean tbh, also the fact that a mere pair of slippers were not provided was a complete let down, I thought the class was 4 stars. So kind of dirty floors and I am supposed to be walking on them barefoot, not an exciting proposition if you ask me.

Finally, I found the walls sort of thin so the sound carried quite a bit but I had ear plugs so I could sleep in the end.

It was a one night stay that I paid 280 euros so it felt a bit underwhelming but not tragic.

data.name: Lindsay
data.pros: I love to stay at this hotel when I visit Paris, because it is great value for what I spend, I like the location in proximity to the Gare du Nord (plus the beautiful view of the Sacre Coeur), and I like the fun/hip vibe of the hotel. It’s very convenient, clean, and the staff are generally friendly. I like the bustling noise outside my window, and if that is very bothersome to you, I would not recommend this hotel. I will definitely be back!

data.name: Stelmakh
data.pros: The breakfast & location was great.
data.cons:
Staff is terrible (actually ony one guy). Apart from the booking payment, you have to pay €8.45 per person per night. That's totally fine.

But the guy at the desk wanted to charge me this tax twice — once during check-in and again during check-out.

It took hours to explain that I had already paid it. Finally, when he realized I had paid it, he requested extra payment for a double room with a single guest, although it is clearly written that the tax is "per person per night", not double for a double room.

Although I wasted 2 hours explaining this, he finally agreed, but said only his manager would be able to refund my initially overpaid €25.35.

What a shame to try to cheat someone out of €25, waste 2 hours of your guest's time, and still not refund my €25 for a stay that cost me around €1,000!!!

data.name: Carsten
data.headline: Toplage, Service ausbaufähig.
data.pros:
Zimmer oben mit Terrasse wirklich sehr schön. Auch hinsichtlich Ausstattung und Zustand der Einrichtung. Kostenloser Kaffee sehr gut. Leise, aber nicht zugfreie Klimaanlage.
Lage absolut top, um Rom zu erkunden. Viel Gastronomie ringsum.
data.cons:
Das Personal war nahe an der Unhöflichkeit. Schon das Einchecken war ein Genuschel und wenig kundenorientiert.
Der Gipfel war dann die Frage beim Auschecken, ob man die Kaution nicht als Tipp für die Angestellten stehenlassen will. Immerhin 60 Euro.
Ich habe dankend verneint. Es war auch das einzige Mal, dass man Mitarbeiter aktiv wahrgenommen hat. Zimmerservice war okay, aber Höflichkeit auf dem Gang auch nicht vorhanden trotz Tipp.
Im TV hunderte Stationen. Aber nur RTL Austria. Bei der Menge an deutschen Gästen in Rom, könnte man sich da mal was einfallen lassen.

data.headline: We loved this hotel and would definitely stay there again.

data.name: Aquilino
data.headline: Absolutely gorgeous amenities and perfect location near the heart of Rome.
data.pros: Location was absolutely perfect right next to the Piazza Navona. The room while not tremendously large was appointed very beautifully. The bathroom was a little bit tight but for downtown Rome it was expected. The lobby was absolutely beautiful as well.
data.cons: We were very disappointed that at no point during our two evening stay that we were able to go to the rooftop bar which was a primary reason why we purchased these rooms. We do understand that there was inclement weather at least on one of the evenings, but when the concierge contacted upstairs to see if we could even go out and see it, we were rejected. Also, on the second day of our stay we had called ahead for a taxi then to find out that even though you called ahead, they couldn't actually call the taxi for you until you were there in the lobby. Even at that point we had to wait a significant amount of time to get the taxi. I don't want this portion of the review to seem like the staff didn't do all that they could to make sure that we were on our way swiftly. However, it would have been nice to know up front that reserving a taxi ahead by calling down does not actually reserve a taxi.

data.name: SLT
data.headline: Lovely hotel in central Rome
data.pros: The location was brilliant, very close to everything. The beds were comfy, we had a triple room and it was spacious enough for the 3 of us. The shower was lovely too. And the breakfast had a good spread of everything. The team at reception were helpful. It was nice to have a roof terrace too.
data.cons: The team on the roof terrace weren't super friendly, but it's separate team to the hotel. It would have been nice for the roof terrace to open at lunchtime, but only a minor detail.

data.name: Virginia
data.headline: Wonderful stay
data.pros: Location was great, breakfast was amazing. Staff arranged for taxi to airport. Many resaurants and shops near by. Easy walk to sights. Large clean room with nice shower. We were on first floor so no view but that was not important to us. Rooftop bar small but nice for a view of city.

data.name: Ayshath
data.headline: Great location
data.pros:
All the staff - excellent. Kind and attentive. 

Breakfast was great.
data.cons:
The smell from the bathroom. I suppose this is due to the drainage in these older buildings. Room cleaning can be better. Often the housekeeping just does a basic job and not really thorough and there is no supervision to check. The laundry bag was taken on the first day and it was never replaced. The used water/wine glasses were not removed for 3 days.

Food at the Mexican can most certainly be improved. Only ordered one meal - was like a microwaved sandwich.

data.headline: Great stay nearly ruined by one rude receptionist

data.cons: Unfortunately our whole stay was nearly ruined by by a very rude lady on reception who when asked if she could sort us a white taxi to the port was really put out, I then asked for a copy of our invoice only to be told she had already given me a copy - This was not the case. It’s a shame we left feeling really annoyed especially as this is not a cheap hotel - manners should be top of the list when dealing with customers and I would not want customers leaving feeling the way we did.

data.name: millomite
data.headline: Noise, no hot water or electricity, no bar, no mini bar, no 24 hour reception
data.pros:
This hotel was selected for a number of reasons. Firstly its location then facilities and finally price.
It is situated on the west side of the Tiber, close to the Vatican, but also a short distance from a bridge across the river. You can easily walk into the main centre and find tourist attractions like the Piazza Navona, Pantheon and Trevi fountain.
If you want to get to, for example, the Colosseum or Forum then the Metro is close by and taxis are not too expensive if there are four in your group (like us). I’d suggest using the Freeform app to book one not Uber.
In the immediate area there are plenty of cafes, restaurants (not too touristy) and little bars. The shops are many and varied if that’s what you want.
Now the interesting part, the hotel. It is not very big and has a 24 hour reception although the one time we needed to contact reception from our room outside of normal hours they never answered the phone! When I went down to see what was the problem  the receptionist was sat reading her phone. I asked her if the phone was working and she looked sheepish and checked it. It was apparently! Forget room service because they obviously don’t have any. You can’t even get a bottle of water from them.
It is advertised as having a bar and also mini bars in the rooms. It has neither. The bar is an empty space in a room near reception and the rooms only have a tiny fridge.
Other issues we and people in our group experienced included:
Room keys continually failing to open the door. This was so bad we asked them to reprogram it every time we walked in to avoid having to come downstairs.
No hot water for showers on so many occasions that I got the manager to move us to another room. Listening in on conversations I conclude this is a widespread problem.
The final straw was when they said the electricity would be switched off from 10pm to 6am! No heating, lighting or lifts. When I said this wasn’t safe in the event of fire (did the fire alarm system work? They said “we think so” lol). We came back early to avoid this potential disaster and get up the five floors in the lift only to discover the power went off 1:30am them came in at 4:30am then off again and only came on properly at 5:30am. We were woken up by this so got a very bad sleep. This was quite literally a disaster waiting to happen and should be reported to the authorities.
A number of other annoyances need to be considered before you book. The hotel is close to a busy road  with cars 24 hours a day and also suffers from very noisy people going home from the bars in the area. Even on the fourth floor (the room we were moved to) it kept us awake most of the night. We bought ear plugs in the end!
The hotel also has large groups of schoolchildren using it with the inevitable noise at night.
The rooms themselves are very dated and lacking in furniture. The curtains were hanging off the rails and the metal blinds could not be raised or lowered. The room was reasonably clean but the bathroom had mould in the corners near the shower and stains in the toilet bowl.
One good point is the breakfast but I’m afraid I will avoid this hotel like the plague for the above reasons.
Continually being told by the staff “it isn’t our problem it’s out of our control” isn’t good enough.

data.name: T528LXsarab
data.headline: A good trip
data.pros:
Great location. Enjoyed being on this side of Rome. Lovely in the evening. Good restaurants and bars nearby - great atmosphere. 
The hotel is fairly basic but clean. The staff at reception were very polite, cheerful and helpful. Breakfast was adequate. There was nothing to complain about. It did the job.

data.name: 626andreaw
data.headline: Not a 4 star hotel.  Disappointing.
data.pros:
No way is this a 4 star hotel. It's a 3 if I'm being generous!  The rooms are basic. Our room had the curtains half hanging off the rail. Room was clean enough and the towels changed daily.  The beds were hard and the pillows , of which we only got 1 each ,weren't much better. The bar that is advertised on the booking sites , wasn't open at all during our entire stay. No irons available at the hotel. Rooms are very noisy with street traffic until around midnight.  
On the plus side it was a nice location. 5 minutes walk to the Vatican.  5 minutes walk to the metro system,  which puts you within easy access anywhere in the city. Lots of nice restaurants  and a couple of nice bars nearby.

data.name: J2053AOamyl
data.headline: Some good points....some bad points
data.pros:
Let's start with the good - good location and friendly knowledgeable staff. Unfortunately that's all I can say about the good.

Bad points - tired, dated, noisy hotel (absolutely no sound proofing) with a basic continental breakfast. 
We had a standard double which was very small and consisted of what I can only describe as camp beds with very hard thin mattresses.  The bathroom was small and had an odd smell.  There are no toiletries or coffee making facilities.  On our first night we had a group of school children screaming,  running,  banging on doors in our corridor.  Eventually by 2am we couldn't take anymore and told them to be quiet and go back to their rooms. We went down to reception to complain....of course no-one was there,  however the teachers responsible for these children were having a lovely time down there, even though they could quite clearly hear the children running wild.  They very quickly went to sort them out! The next morning we complained to the staff and they immediately changed our room and gave us a bottle of wine as an apology.  Our next room was much better but once again basic and the smell from the bathroom was worse than the room before. The hotel building is a lovely old building which is slowly being modernised, however the decoration does look a bit shabby in places.  If and when done properly I'm sure this hotel would be stunning. Whilst we appreciate this hotel is in a good location in a world famous capital city the room rate they charge, for the standard they provide, is pretty extortionate. 
Breakfast was once again basic,  coffee and juices weak....but croissants fresh and tasty.
We're not ones to normally complain but on this occasion we felt we needed to say something and thankfully the helpful staff did sort out our problem. They now just need to enhance their service, standards and facilities to reflect the price they charge and it would be a lovely hotel.

data.name: 986DMFL
data.headline: Extremely disappointing stay
data.pros:
I shared a twin room at the Grand Olympic Hotel in Rome in November 2025 for one night and was extremely disappointed with my experience. This property is advertised as a four-star hotel, but the room assigned (Room 56, ground floor) didn’t meet even the most basic standards of cleanliness or maintenance.  

There was a heavy grill on the outside of the window which was immoveable and could not be adjusted.   There were no window coverings at all on the inside of the window and we had to rely on this grill for any and all privacy.  By morning we found out the metal grill restricted 95% of all natural daylight in the room with a terrible view through the slats of a storage/rubbish area outside.  On realising the grill was fixed I did wonder what would happen in the event of a fire as the grill operated as a permanent obstruction which is very unusual to find on the ground floor of any hotel as it creates a potential entrapment space in the room if a fire occurred.  On searching I found absolutely no guest evacuation instructions in the room at all which I would suggest is a compliance issue under health and safety regulations.   On the inside of the room entrance door was a no smoking sign poorly fixed to the door but nothing else [see pictures].  On the inside of the bathroom door was a generic technicians service label for fire equipment that was incomplete and not something that should be guest facing as it offered no useful information in the event of a fire for guests.  It referenced door 106 which I assume is the nearest fire door but not on our level.

The room itself was filthy and needed a deep clean.  The air-conditioning unit was leaking, leaving water stains all down the wall with mold present and a smell of damp which was accompanied by the smell of the drain in the shower.  This issue had clearly been there a considerable amount of time without being addressed.    There was accumulated dirt along the skirting, hair and dirt on the floor belonging to previous occupants.  The walls were full of scuff marks.  The spotlights on the ceiling were carelessly overpainted.  Overall, the room felt neglected, dirty and badly maintained.

The second bed had no headboard and was made up with only a sheet and a light cover [about the same thickness as the sheet]. There was no duvet or warm covering at all and nothing available in the room.  Meanwhile, the first bed did have a light duvet, making the inconsistency even more noticeable.

The bathroom was no better: the main drench shower head was scaled over and clearly hadn’t been cleaned in a long time, and the shower gel dispenser was empty, not even an empty soap cartridge.  

The clothes wardrobe was damaged to the point where it blocked the fridge, making it impossible to open the fridge door. There was no security safe, no in room tea or coffee facilities or any extra pillows, blankets or coverings. The TV remote had masking tape wrapped around it to hold the batteries in because the back cover was missing.

Dust was thick on surfaces; one swipe of my finger across the bedside locker left a clear line and covered my fingers in dust and dirt.

When I contacted reception, I was passed to an English-speaking off duty staff member by phone. I asked to move rooms but was told the hotel was fully booked. I then asked for housekeeping to attend to the room but was informed that nothing could be done until morning as there was only the receptionist on duty and the room had been cleaned and the team were good at their job so there was no problem.       I  offered to clean the room myself if they would provide supplies rather than stay there as it was, but this was refused.

When the receptionist visited the room,  I asked about the missing duvet and was told to “turn on the heater,” despite the unit obviously leaking and surrounded by mold. Eventually, the receptionist fetched a duvet from another room, but even that had visible stains to match the stains on the bed coverings.  Whilst refusing to help with the most basic of things we were then asked to contact reception if there was anything we needed!

The next morning, the sink and shower had no hot water at all. Everything ran cold.  Not even a hot water kettle in the room so we had to make do with cold water.  No apologies from the hotel staff, not even a recognition there was a problem with the room.

The only positive was the location. Otherwise, the cleanliness, room condition, and complete lack of staff support made this stay unacceptable. I have no issue with basic accommodation, but I expect it to be clean, safe, and functional. This room was none of those things, and it certainly did not reflect the standards of a four-star hotel which we paid for.  I would not recommend this hotel in any way and that is unfortunate as it’s a great location.  Had the hotel tried to make any efforts at all to rectify the situation I would not have made this post but they completely dismissed any problems with the room.

data.headline: Lovely hotel
data.pros:
Lovely hotel, had everything we needed for the one night. 
Be careful with the shower, the water leaks out from under the door, don’t put anything near there you wouldn’t want to get wet! 
Make sure you take a form of photo ID, I didn’t realise you would need it. 
Breakfast was really nice, plenty of choice and the restaurant is huge so plenty of space no matter what time you go.

data.name: W8642HPannem
data.headline: Don’t stay here
data.pros:
This is the worst hotel I’ve ever stayed at , and we’ve stayed at many many hotels around the world . 

The only thing going for it is the location and breakfast .

We found the staff to be extremely rude and unhelpful , we had multiple stays in a matters of weeks with them and if we hadn’t of pre paid we would have cancelled our booking after the 1 st stay . 
The rooms are tidy but there is nothing in the room but a bed and a chair . I’m sorry this is classed as a 4.5 star hotel they don’t even have a restaurant and the bar is a little cafe outside which charge £9 for 2 small bottles of water !!!!
My husband was having a shower ( pretty crappy shower,  great if you have disabilities ) and the entire bathroom flooded . There is no shower stall
It’s open with a curtain that doesn’t even reach the floor. The tap
In the tiny sink had to be held up with one hand whilst trying to get your hands washed 
We had a 3 day get away and we were booked to come back and we asked them if they would store our larger  bags for us if possible , we were told nope it can’t happen , so we had to spend another £50 to store our bags at a storage place , maybe I’m being unreasonable but if we had had  3 stays in a short time each for between 2-4 days each stay that maybe they would be a little accomodating in helping us . 
There is limited places to sit and relax unless you sit outside on the kerb .. 

We stayed at the RIU in Dublin and it was fantastic , the staff, the bar,
the restaurant the rooms where all lovely 
Such a shame that the RIU Westminster couldn’t be like them .
 I’m not one to write a review but I wanted to warn anyone thinking of staying here to reconsider and maybe find a better 4.5 star hotel which actually looks after their patrons

data.name: Alicurts
data.headline: Riu Westminster London
data.pros:
This was my first stay at the Hotel Riu Plaza London The Westminster, and overall, I found the hotel to be pleasant and accommodating.

From the moment we arrived, the lobby staff were friendly, helpful, and sociable. The check-in process was quick and efficient. Although we arrived before our room was ready, the staff gladly stored our luggage so that we could begin enjoying London without having to carry our bags around.

Our room was on the smaller side, but it was perfectly adequate for our stay. It included a small refrigerator, the air conditioning worked very well, and there was always plenty of hot water. Overall, the room was comfortable and met our needs.

Breakfast was average, with a decent selection but nothing particularly extraordinary. One suggestion I would make is to offer mimosas during breakfast, even if they are available for an additional charge. As someone who enjoys a mimosa with breakfast while on vacation, I would have happily paid separately for one.

Unfortunately, I did have one uncomfortable experience during breakfast that I feel is worth mentioning. An employee repeatedly hovered around my guest and me while we were eating and remained nearby until we finished. What made the situation particularly noticeable was that the same level of attention was not given to a white family of four seated nearby who had finished their meal before we did.

As people of color, we could not help but feel singled out by the difference in treatment. I cannot speak to the employee’s intentions, but the experience made us uncomfortable and gave us the impression that we were being watched more closely than other guests. Perhaps additional training regarding consistent and equitable treatment of all guests would be beneficial.

That experience aside, the remainder of our stay was pleasant. The hotel is comfortable, the lobby staff made a very positive impression, and I appreciated the overall service we received.

I would stay at the Hotel Riu Plaza London The Westminster again on a future visit to London. I simply hope that management takes concerns such as this seriously so that every guest feels equally welcomed and comfortable throughout their stay.

data.name: YannickVH
data.headline: Avoid booking directly via RIU
data.pros:
In general, I would say that this hotel is decent for a stay in London if their service were more customer-centric. Our room was far from perfect: there was mold next to the shower, and the wood next to the shower was swollen as well. The sink had green algae and was broken. During breakfast, we asked for a gluten-free brownie. It didn’t taste well, and when checking the expiration date, we discovered that the brownie was already expired for two days. The taste might not be due to the expiration, but a hotel (and certainly not a 4* hotel) shouldn’t serve expired food to customers. These issues were discussed with the hotel staff. They direct you to a general email address for complaints. In return for these inconveniences, we were offered 1500 RIU Class points. To be honest, I don’t think this is fair compensation. When you book directly via Riu, you would think they appreciate this more and would offer a compensation in the currency (money) you paid, not in some virtual points which in the real world don’t have value. I asked to be compensated in the currency of our booking, but sadly enough, the helpdesk employee again replied that the points are the only way they can compensate.

So in short: we would think twice about booking this hotel again. Be aware that some rooms in RIU are outdated and need maintenance, check expiration dates on the gluten-free food, and place your booking via a third party like Booking.com since you will be compensated in a correct way and not in a virtual currency that has no real value. The complaints handling is a joke for these serious mistakes.

data.name: kerry
data.headline: Good hotel - let down by one issue not dealt with correctly.
data.pros:
Location. Very clean and big hotel. 
Check in staff were great. 
Lovely welcoming atmosphere.
data.cons:
Upon returning to room after being out I had noticed my laptop bag had been opened and the room smelled of weed. 
I reported this to the duty manager immediately who came to the room with the member of staff that had been in to do the turn down. 
The staff member said they did not go through the bag and I had obviously left it open.
As two females, we felt very intimidated and it was being made we were making it up. 
Although we did get moved due to the smell, the cups and spoons were dirty but we did not feel as though we could report this. 

As a hotel manager myself, this situation could have been dealt with very different and we would have had a totally different experience.

data.name: Lucy
data.headline: Very disappointing
data.pros: Good location
data.cons: On 23-24 October 2026, our key card failed in the lift and we were prompted to leave it and find another route. A housekeeper had to let us into a stairwell with her key card, but none of the doors would open from inside, so we were trapped in a service area with only an alarmed fire exit as a way out. We got out only by pressing a call button for security and phoning reception. This is a real safety hazard, and stairs should be accessible, clearly signposted and always usable. The duty manager's office offered a free breakfast, which we declined as inadequate. I emailed the hotel and received an apology and a promise of an internal review, but have heard nothing since, even after following up. Management's silence on a safety issue is disappointing.

data.pros: This hotel is in a great location with good views across the Thames from our room and trendy/ interesting decor. Expresso coffee was good. Injured my knee and staff at the bar near the Thames exit/ Lyaness entry were outstanding in providing ice and assistance.
data.cons: Rooms are light on storage (absolutely none) but were very comfortable. Check-in on a Friday afternoon was a little average with no assistance getting luggage from the street into the hotel or to our room. A challenge using the revolving doors with four bags. There were no instruction at check-in on facilities, dining options or on accessing roomservice (through the TV) despite we being the only party checking in at the time (not busy).  Breakfast buffet was was good although with limited bread choices, unreplenished meats, no smoked salmon, etc).

data.name: Linda
data.headline: We will be thinking and talking about our stay at the Londoner for quite some time. It was great!
data.pros:
We used the residents lounge for breakfast after our first morning and very much enjoyed the relaxed atmosphere and the attention of the staff. It was very good value for money compared to Whitcombs. We also had dinner there one evening and found it a nice place to have a drink at various times of the day.
We loved the location of the hotel for visiting the National gallery and Portrait gallery. Also a short taxi ride from theatres and restaurants. We enjoyed the Japanese cocktail bar. Though expensive, it was an unusual treat. A very nice space and the views were fabulous. We also enjoyed drinks at the champagne bar a couple of times. 
We loved the pool area and spa - the best massage I have ever had!
data.cons: Not keen on Whitcombs or the Tavern - both were noisy with loud music playing. Breakfast at Whitcombs was not relaxing - the tables are too close together. We had planned to have dinner there one evening but changed our minds after experiencing breakfast there.

data.name: Marina Lua Abreu
data.headline: Hospedagem moderna
data.pros: Prédio moderno, com estudios com uma pequena cozinha que da pra resolver pequenas refeicoes, fechamos com cafe da manhã que é bem farto. O staff muito bacana, tivemos problema com as chaves e conseguimos solucionar. Deram um mimo por ser nossa lua de mel, mas a vista do quarto não era muito boa, e isso era o principal para nós. o quarto é grande, moderno. O predio é no mesmo quarteirao da estacao aldgate east. Vizinhança boa. Não tivemos early check in, mas fomos acolhidos com chá e cafe, além de guardar as malas. Tem agua de graca no frigobar e da pra reabastacer a garrafa de vidro na lavanderia do predio prox a academia.
data.cons: Não conseguimos espelhar a tv no sistema do hotel. No ultimo dia do cafe da manha a cafeteira profissional não funcionou. A limpeza nos quartos só acontece depois de 3 dias, sentimos falta.

data.name: Petra
data.headline: Velmi pěkný hotel
data.pros:
Pokoje jsou velmi dobře a vkusně zařízené. Vše čisté, kuchyňka zařízená základním vybavením, ale dostatečně pro svačiny i lehčí večeři.  
Postel je menší (užší) s jednou velkou teplou peřinou, dva druhy polštářů. Akorát tvrdá/měkká matrace. 
Pokoj byl v 11 patře a byl zde klid. V noci je možné slyšet houkající policii nebo motorku, ale nic hrozného. Prostě klasický hluk rušnější ulice. 
Koupelna pěkně zařízená. Šampon, kondicionér, mýdlo i krém jsou součástí vybavení. Ve sprše byl trochu slabší tlak vody, ale v 11 patře se to dá očekávat. Nebylo to nic hrozného. 
Poloha je skvělá. Hned vedle hotelu jsou samoobsluhy, restaurace/bar, kavárny. Několik desítek metrů metro. Od Tower Bridge asi 10 minut pěšky.

data.name: Banu
data.headline: Excellent
data.pros:
We were extremely pleased with our stay at the hotel. The staff were always attentive, helpful, and friendly. The breakfast was more than sufficient and delicious. The cleanliness of the hotel also exceeded our expectations.

I would especially like to point out that, unlike many hotels, there were no unnecessary decorative cushions or bedspreads on the beds, which we found particularly reassuring in terms of hygiene and cleanliness.

The hotel is located in a very pleasant and upscale neighborhood, and its accessibility was excellent. There was a metro station and a bus stop directly across from the hotel, as well as a supermarket and a pharmacy nearby for everyday essentials.

Overall, we had a wonderful stay and would definitely recommend this hotel!
data.cons: I wish there would be a mirror on the vanity and coffee desk.

data.name: Tabea
data.headline: Sehr gute zentrale Lage
data.pros: Die Lage ist genial. Die Angestellten waren sehr hilfsbereit und haben sich sofort um den Ersatz der defekten Lampe und eine Heizung gekümmert.
data.cons: Lage des Appartements zum Innenhof brachte abends sehr viel Lärm vom Pub in der Nähe. Die Ausstattung mit Besteck war sehr rudimentär mit 2 Löffeln und 2 Messern. Wasserkocher wäre komfortabel gewesen. Die Dusche war etwas klein und unansehnlich.

data.name: Silke Brändle
data.headline: Top Lage und freundliches Personal, aber die Wohnung ist stark abgewohnt.
data.pros:
Die Lage der Unterkunft ist wirklich hervorragend. Sie befindet sich in einem netten Viertel in unmittelbarer Nähe zum Leadenhall Market und zur Tower Bridge. In der Umgebung gibt es zahlreiche Bars, Restaurants und Einkaufsmöglichkeiten.

Auch die Verkehrsanbindung ist ausgezeichnet. Eine Zug- und U-Bahn-Station befindet sich in unmittelbarer Nähe. Besonders praktisch ist die direkte Anbindung an den Stansted Express.

Die Rezeption ist rund um die Uhr besetzt. Da wir bereits sehr früh angereist waren, konnten wir unser Gepäck problemlos dort lassen. Die Mitarbeiter waren durchwegs freundlich, hilfsbereit und sehr bemüht, unseren Aufenthalt so angenehm wie möglich zu gestalten.
data.cons:
Die Wohnung war leider insgesamt in einem sehr abgewohnten und renovierungsbedürftigen Zustand. Natürlich erwartet man in London nicht überall einen luxuriösen Standard, aber bei diesem Preis hätten wir uns deutlich mehr erwartet.

Besonders enttäuschend war das Badezimmer. Die Fliesen waren verfärbt, teilweise gelöst und die Fugen stark abgenutzt. Das gesamte Bad machte einen heruntergekommenen Eindruck.

Auch die Fenster waren verschmutzt und die Bettwäsche war bei unserer Ankunft fleckig und musste erst ausgetauscht werden. Der Fernseher funktionierte zunächst ebenfalls nicht und musste repariert werden.

Der Ausblick aus dem Schlafzimmer war ebenfalls alles andere als schön und trug nicht gerade zum Wohlfühlgefühl bei.

Zwar war die Wohnung grundsätzlich sauber geputzt, allerdings kann Sauberkeit den offensichtlichen Renovierungsbedarf und den schlechten Zustand der Einrichtung nicht ausgleichen.

Besonders ärgerlich ist, dass auf den Fotos der Zwei-Zimmer-Wohnung kein Badezimmer zu sehen war. Im Nachhinein ist klar, warum. Die Fotos vermitteln insgesamt einen deutlich besseren Eindruck, als die Unterkunft tatsächlich bietet.

Unsere wichtigste Erkenntnis aus dieser Erfahrung: Wir werden künftig keine Unterkunft mehr buchen, bei der das Badezimmer auf den Fotos nicht zu sehen ist.

Insgesamt stimmten Zustand, Ausstattung und Preis für uns leider überhaupt nicht überein.

data.name: Radu
data.headline: An overpriced stay with poor cleanliness, worn facilities, and disappointing service.
data.pros: Location
data.cons:
Unfortunately, this hotel damages the reputation of the otherwise well-regarded Mövenpick brand. It gives the impression of relying on strong demand and the Mövenpick name to charge high prices, while paying very little attention to service quality.

Despite the extremely high price for a single night, I had to queue at reception just to get slippers. The toilet seat was damaged and stained, the tissue box was empty, and the carpet was stained and had not been thoroughly cleaned. There was also an empty water bottle behind the television, presumably left by a previous guest. The furniture was worn and showed clear signs of deterioration.

I did not receive an invoice at checkout. I was told it would be emailed to me, but it never arrived.

Based on my experience, the hotel does not live up to its four-star rating or its prices. The relevant rating authority should reassess its classification.

data.name: Iris
data.headline: Ein angenehmes Hotel als Ausgangspunkt Ansterdam zu erkunden.
data.pros: Das Hotel macht einen sauberen und gepflegten Eindruck. Das Personal ist sehr zuvorkommend. Unser Auto war in der Tiefgarage gut aufgehoben. Direkt vor dem Hotel befindet sich eine Metrostation. Trotz der Lage ist  das Hotelzimmer sehr ruhig. Wir hatten im obersten Stock einen super Ausblick. Das Frühstücksangebot war sehr vielfältig mit warmen und kalten Speisen und einer Kuchenauswahl. Auch verschiedene Teesorten waren verfügbar. Genügend Platz bzw. Tische waren ebenfalls vorhanden.
data.cons: Nur eine Kleinigkeit. Mir persönlich war das Kopfkissen etwas zu hart bzw. zu stark gefüllt.

data.name: Trek402026
data.headline: Luxury service at the highest level
data.pros:
Great care is given to all guests.  When I arrived the front desk checked me in immediately and when I requested help with a dinner reservation pre-arrival they arranged a spot for me at the Yamazato Restaurant, a Michelin 1 star.  While it was listed as full they double checked the waitlist and found a cancellation that evening. Amazing service, the 23rd floor bar staff was fabulous.  The restaurant was top marks. Wine, food and service was on par with what I expected.  The manager who I remember from 8 years ago checked w/me halfway through service, he noticed I loved the sashimi and brought me another piece of Chutoro, tasted fabulous , the dinner was delicious.  Sommelier was amazing w/wine selection for the evening.  They upgraded my room as I was a leaders club member to a beautiful corner room.  I also needed to find a pharmacy last minute and Rochelle at the front deck was very helpful in locating one for me.  Just wonderful service all around.  Great job team!
Im really looking forward to coming again.

data.name: mixedhappy_family5
data.headline: A++++ for food, staff, design.
data.pros:
We stayed at Hotel Okura Amsterdam from Tuesday to Saturday and had the most beautifully relaxed experience. From the moment we arrived, everything felt effortless and welcoming.

The food was excellent throughout our stay. We dined at both restaurants and were truly impressed by the quality, presentation, and flavour. Every meal felt special. We also spent time at the top-floor bar, where the views are absolutely stunning. The scenery alone is worth the visit, but the cocktails made it even better — perfectly crafted and thoughtfully chosen by the incredibly talented bar staff.

What truly sets this hotel apart is the service. Every single member of staff was exceptional — from the doormen and receptionists to the breakfast team, bar staff, cleaners, porters, and restaurant staff. Everyone was warm, professional, and genuinely attentive. It’s rare to experience such consistently high standards across the board.

The spa was another highlight. The atmosphere was calm and luxurious, and the team there were wonderful. I had a facial with Sarah, who was fantastic — professional, skilled, and so relaxing. Mya at the spa reception was incredibly welcoming and helpful, making the whole experience seamless from start to finish.

It’s definitely a place we would return to without hesitation. It’s perfect for a relaxing getaway, and it’s lovely to see that children are also welcome, making it suitable for families too.

A truly exceptional stay from beginning to end.

data.name: godelieve
data.headline: Our first stay at Hotel Okura
data.pros:
We recently stayed for two nights at Hotel Okura and had a very pleasant experience.
One detail we especially appreciated was how quiet the elevators were — it made a noticeable difference in the overall calm atmosphere of the hotel. Our junior suite was comfortable and well-appointed, with a very good bed and pillows that ensured restful nights.

The housekeeping team was attentive and thorough, and we consistently found the room in excellent condition. Overall, the personnel were exceptionally friendly, welcoming, and attentive throughout our stay.

We also enjoyed spending time at the bar.

Thank you for a comfortable and relaxing stay — we would be happy to return.

data.name: renetI7767WP
data.headline: The okura experience
data.pros:
During our stay at Hotel Okura Amsterdam, we had a truly wonderful experience. From the moment we arrived until our departure, everything was impeccably arranged and thoughtfully taken care of.

A very special thank you goes to Concierge Nigel Winklaar, whose exceptional attention and professionalism made our stay effortless and memorable. From our room and overall service to the spa, dinner, and breakfast — every detail was perfectly coordinated.

The level of personal care, warmth, and precision we experienced is rare. This stay was not only comfortable, but genuinely special.

Thank you for an outstanding experience. We look forward to returning.

data.name: David
data.headline: Bedankt, Raisa!
data.pros:
Overall, everything was good. The property is nice, although the rooms are very small. The location is excellent, with everything within easy reach.

I would recommend paying a little more attention to cleanliness in the shared areas, as there is some room for improvement.

A special thank you to a staff member named Raisa. She is absolutely wonderful! Very friendly, kind, and welcoming. People like her make a stay much more enjoyable.

⸻

Over het algemeen was alles prima. Het verblijf is prettig, hoewel de kamers erg klein zijn. De locatie is uitstekend en alles is gemakkelijk bereikbaar.

Ik zou wel aanraden om wat meer aandacht te besteden aan de netheid van de gemeenschappelijke ruimtes, want daar is nog ruimte voor verbetering.

Een speciaal woord van dank aan een medewerkster genaamd Raisa. Ze is werkelijk fantastisch! Ontzettend vriendelijk, aardig en gastvrij. Mensen zoals zij maken een verblijf zoveel aangenamer.

⸻

Insgesamt war alles gut. Die Unterkunft ist schön, allerdings sind die Zimmer sehr klein. Die Lage ist ausgezeichnet und alles ist gut erreichbar.

Bei der Sauberkeit in den Gemeinschaftsbereichen würde ich empfehlen, etwas genauer hinzuschauen, da es hier noch Verbesserungspotenzial gibt.

Ein besonderes Dankeschön geht an die Mitarbeiterin Raisa. Sie ist einfach wunderbar! Sehr freundlich, herzlich und hilfsbereit. Menschen wie sie machen einen Aufenthalt deutlich angenehmer.

data.name: pereira
data.headline: Hôtel historique mais personnel mal formés.
data.pros: L'emplacement est très agréable et proche des centres cultures comme l'opéra, musées et salle de concert. L'hôtel dispose en effet de belles installations et d'un charme des années 40.
data.cons: Le service à l'enregistrement et au départ a été déplorable. Les personnes à la réception n'avaient pas les compétences nécessaires et cela a provoqué beaucoup d'erreurs de prélèvements bancaires. Trois jours après mon départ, je devais encore écrire à leur comptable pour régler un remboursement des frais indument prélevés sur mon compte. De plus l'attente à la réception a été longue ; il fallait faire la queue débout devant la réception pour ne pas perdre voter tour. Un vrai désastre.

data.pros: המיקום מעולה, ארוחת בוקר טובה ומגוונת, הצוות מאוד נחמד
data.cons: מעלית אחת לאגף שהיינו, נמצאת בחדר צדדי, נראה כאילו חלק אחורי של מלון- תחושה מאוד לא נעימה. בגלל שיש מעלית אחת לעיתים נאלצנו לחכות הרבה זמן למעלית בבוקר. חדר רחצה ישן, יש עובש במקלחת, את המרכך שנגמר לא החליפו ולא שמו מספיק נייר טואלט, נאלצנו להתקשר שיביאו לנו. היינו בחדר סוויטה ג'וניור עם שתי מיטות, היו אלה שתי מיטות יחיד קטנות, עם שמיכות קטנות, לא אמור להיות ברמה כזו במחיר כזה ובסוג חדר כזה- מאכזב!!

data.name: Olga
data.headline: Creative and fashionable
data.pros: I have stayed at this hotel many times and absolutely love it for its aesthetics, atmosphere, and history. It did not disappoint me this time either. A beautiful room, a comfortable bed, a delicious breakfast that is absolutely worth the price, attentive and caring reception staff, and a lovely bar downstairs — all contributed to another wonderful stay.
data.cons:
For a hotel of this calibre, I would expect basic amenities such as slippers and vanity kits to be provided in the room. 
Also, despite having stayed here many times, I have only just discovered that the hotel actually has a wellness area! There is virtually no information about it anywhere, and the reception team is not particularly helpful when it comes to explaining what is available. The response was something along the lines of, “Oh yes, we do have one. Just let us know when you’re planning to go, and we’ll get everything ready.” I would really appreciate some information about the wellness facilities being made available in advance — perhaps through a brochure or a dedicated section on the website. It would be much nicer to be able to read about the facilities and decide whether to use them comfortably, rather than having to go there and investigate everything myself.

data.headline: Lieblos und heruntergewohnt
data.pros:
Bequeme Betten
Für uns gute Lage
data.cons:
Ausstattung Küche extrem schlecht - nur ein Topf ohne Deckel. Auch auf Rückfrage dauerte es zwei Tage bis wir einen Topf und eine Pfanne hatten. 
In der Küche nur kaltes Wasser.
Zwei Fernseher in der Unterkunft - aber keiner davon smart und viele Programmplätze sind nicht belegt.

Dauerhafte Unbauarbeiten in anderen Appartements - Durchgängiger Bohrlärm, auch samstags.

Kommunikation mit der Unterkunft läuft teils über einen AI Assistenten - der regelt aber nix und gibt nur generische Antworten.

Alles in allem leider keine gute Erfahrung, wir werden beim nächsten Besuch in Berlin woanders wohnen.

data.name: Jennifer
data.headline: Unresolved Issues, Unsafe Practices, and Poor Comm
data.pros: Numa finally contacted me after my review on Google (which is below) they’ve offered 20% refund which is still pending as they said it would take 10-14 days. Review: “If there is an issue, they will not be able to resolve it timely or respond. (1) AC was out in my mother’s room the entire 5 day stay and it was a very hot weekend. All they offered was 30% refund after days of no status or responding to us. (2) the essentials closet was empty so no towels for a day. They said they would drop some off the next day. (3) they dropped off the towels BUT LEFT OUR ROOM DOOR WIDE OPEN WITH OUR BELONGINGS EXPOSED!! Absolutely unacceptable for any accommodation!! They told me multiple times over WhatsApp that safety was trip priority and someone would contact me in 10-15 minutes… that never happened! I do not recommend Numa Berlin for long term stays or safety reasons.”

data.name: Francisco
data.pros: Great place to stay

data.name: Todd
data.pros: The worst experience that i have had. No AC and was told daily they would fix it.  They never did.  Shower leaks water out of the small confined area.  Asked for clean towels and didn’t receive until after 24 hours.  No towels in the essential closet.  There was not enough room for two people to have luggage and move around in the room at the same time.  The TV would not let us stream even though they said it would.  Only one chair at the desk to sit in and it was at the foot of the bed upstairs.  I have no idea why they gave us this room as we ordered a medium room and was billed for a medium room.  We are expecting a 30% refund but have yet to receive it.  I will be taking this further to the management to get a full refund for all of the inconveniences and accommodations that lacked.

data.name: Joe
data.pros:
We had an absolutely wonderful stay at Hotel President in Prague! The staff were incredibly friendly and welcoming, making us feel at home from the moment we arrived. Their warmth and hospitality truly made our stay special.

Everything was excellent—from our beautiful room and the delicious breakfast to the wellness facilities and gym. All the facilities were in immaculate condition, and the warm, friendly atmosphere throughout the hotel made it easy to relax and enjoy every moment.

Thank you to the entire team for such a memorable stay. We can’t wait to return and would wholeheartedly recommend this hotel to anyone visiting Prague!

data.name: ΝΙΚΟΛΑΟΣ
data.pros:
We had a wonderful stay at Pytloun Boutique Hotel Prague with our family. Everything exceeded our expectations!

The breakfast was, without a doubt, the best I have ever experienced at a hotel, offering an amazing variety and outstanding quality. The hotel's location is fantastic, with easy access to Prague's Old Town and the metro, making it the perfect base for exploring the city.

The hotel facilities are excellent, and the entire staff deserves special praise for their professionalism, friendliness, and outstanding hospitality.

A very special mention goes to Karoline, who went above and beyond to make sure our family had a truly memorable and exceptional stay. Her kindness, attention to detail, and willingness to help made all the difference.

We couldn't have asked for a better experience. Highly recommended, and we would definitely love to come back!

data.name: Tommaso
data.headline: Ottima struttura a pochi passi dal centro della città e in posizione tranquilla
data.pros: L'albergo si trova a pochi passi dal centro della città vecchia e dalle principali attrattive, raggiungibili a piedi nel giro di pochi minuti eccezion fatta per il castello per il quale è necessario prendere un bus la cui fermata è a pochi minuti di cammino. La camera che ci hanno assegnato era una ampia quadrupla composta da due stanze comunicanti, fornita di ampio bagno e finestre sulla strada che, sebbene centrale, era silenziosa sia di giorno che di notte. Buona la colazione, sia continentale che "italiana", servita in una sala al quarto piano e in una fascia oraria abbastanza estesa che non obbliga a svegliarsi presto al mattino.
data.cons: Le finestre andrebbero oscurate meglio: le tende al mattino lasciano filtrare un po' di luce che può essere fastidiosa per chi ha il sonno leggero.

data.pros: Great location.  Very safe and lots of excellent bars and restaurants nearby.

data.name: Sharon
data.pros: Great hotel for a city break. My only issue was construction noise coming from the building behind the hotel that my window looked onto, lots of power tool noise from builders that went on until 9pm some days, I prefer to have the window open but I had to shut it which blocked a lot of the volume. My double room was quite spacious and well equipped, bed was comfortable, breakfast buffet had a lot of options and tasty and well laid out.  Location is brilliant, right by the Ujezd tram stop, but also very walkable for Lesser Town and even Old Town if you like to walk.  There are restaurants within walking distance, I didn't find a supermarket but there is a very expensive mini-grocery around the corner towards the bridge. I would stay here again.  I also took advantage of the hotel private transfer since I was arriving late evening, friendly English speaking driver brought be straight from the airport to the hotel.

data.name: Helena
data.headline: Short stay in Hilton
data.pros:
The location is nice. 
The fact that pets can be brought is nice. 
Spaa is nice.
data.cons: My mistake of course completely that I didn’t check that parking fee for guests is so high and that spa visiting time ends for kids under 16 starting from 19pm so we arrived with my daughter 18:20 and we came mostly also because of the spa but then had to rush to the room to change and got to enjoy it only half an hour. We came after school and work day so earliest check in was not possible but well for me it was one not so good discovery after another. In some other hotel spas one can stay w kid way longer, I automatically thought it’s the case here. The soft furniture - canapé in the room had also stains, maybe it’s possible to check or remove them time to time with specific machines for such fabrics, because all I was seeing was stained furniture where I would not want to sit.

data.cons: No vanity kit? Is that a new Hilton standard?

data.name: Olga
data.headline: A beautiful historic hotel in an exceptional location. A truly wonderful experience!
data.pros:
A wonderful hotel! We had a beautiful room, and I loved the hotel’s elegant interiors, historic character, and exceptional location right in the heart of the Old Town.

A special mention goes to the Tchaikovsky restaurant, where we had both breakfast and dinner. It was absolutely excellent. I particularly appreciated the variety of local dishes and regional products offered at breakfast. The restaurant itself is also incredibly elegant. 
I was also extremely impressed by the staff’s attentiveness. Every request I had made in advance was carefully taken into account and fulfilled exactly as I had wished.
data.cons: Nothing. Everything was wonderful!

data.name: Erkka
data.headline: Otherwise excellent but an off day at the spa
data.pros: Everything from the staff to the amenities were excellent. We especially enjoyed the spa facilities.
data.cons:
We’ve visited the hotel and its spa often and have always enjoyed it. On our most recent visit, a number of children were making a lot of noise in the spa area one evening. Kids will be kids, and the responsibility for supervising them lies with the adults in charge, but the screaming and shouting carried all the way to reception. When I mentioned it to the trainee on duty, unfortunately nothing was done, and she didn’t come into the spa area until most of the customers had left. Her reaction to my complaint did not make me feel heard or appreciated, meanwhile it was obvious also from other customers faces that the spa was not an enjoyable experience. In the meantime, there were no water glasses left out and the towels on the sunbeds hadn’t been changed.

This made me wonder why a trainee was left on her own to handle the spa at a busy time. This was very unusual compared with our previous visits, and it was especially disappointing as the relaxing spa moments are the reason we keep returning. Perhaps some designated family times could help keep the spa relaxing for everyone.

pages.title: What's on in Lisbon in November 2026
pages.text: Lisbon in November 2026: the São Martinho chestnut festival on 11 November with roasted chestnuts and água-pé across the city; Web Summit at the MEO Arena from 9 to 12 November, when hotels in Parque das Nações fill up; the Lisbon & Sintra Film Festival from 13 to 22 November; and Fado nights every evening in Alfama and Mouraria.

pages.title: Getting around Lisbon: metro, trams and the airport
pages.text: The red metro line runs from Lisbon airport to the city in about 20 minutes; change at Alameda for the green line to Baixa-Chiado. A single ticket costs EUR 1.85 on a Navegante card. Tram 28 runs from Martim Moniz through Graça, Alfama and Chiado to Estrela; board early to avoid queues. A taxi from the airport to Baixa costs about EUR 15–20.

pages.title: A day trip to Sintra from Lisbon
pages.text: Trains to Sintra leave Rossio station every 20 minutes and take 40 minutes. Pena Palace opens 9:30 to 18:30 and timed tickets (EUR 20) sell out in high season; the Quinta da Regaleira opens 10:00 to 18:00. Take bus 434 from Sintra station up the hill.

pages.title: Where to eat in Baixa and Chiado
pages.text: In Chiado, Manteigaria bakes pastéis de nata all day; in Baixa, the Time Out Market at Cais do Sodré gathers 40 kitchens under one roof (10:00–24:00). For dinner, Cervejaria Ramiro is famous for seafood; expect a queue after 19:30.

pages.title: Three days in Porto: a first-timer's plan
pages.text: Day 1: Ribeira, the Dom Luís I bridge and the port wine lodges in Vila Nova de Gaia (Graham's and Taylor's offer tours from EUR 25). Day 2: Livraria Lello (timed tickets EUR 10, opens 9:00), Clérigos Tower, Bolhão market and a francesinha for lunch. Day 3: a Douro river cruise of the six bridges (50 minutes, EUR 18) and sunset at Jardim do Morro.

pages.title: Porto in December 2026: Christmas markets and New Year
pages.text: The Porto Christmas market runs on Avenida dos Aliados from 28 November 2026 to 6 January 2027, open 10:00 to 22:00. The city lights are switched on on 28 November. Many restaurants close on 24 and 25 December; book ahead.

pages.title: Porto airport to the city centre
pages.text: Metro line E (violet) runs from the airport to Trindade in 30 minutes; a Z4 Andante ticket costs EUR 2.60. A taxi or ride-hail to Ribeira costs about EUR 25. Trains to Lisbon leave from Campanhã; the Alfa Pendular takes 2 h 50 min.

pages.title: Porto food guide: francesinha, port and petiscos
pages.text: Café Santiago and Bufete Fase serve the best-known francesinhas. For port tastings, Vila Nova de Gaia's lodges open 10:00 to 18:00. Book Cantinho do Avillez in Baixa a week ahead.

pages.title: Lisbon in December 2026: Christmas lights, markets and Wonderland Lisboa
pages.text: Lisbon's Christmas lights switch on in late November 2026 across Baixa, Chiado and Avenida da Liberdade, with a giant tree in Praça do Comércio. Wonderland Lisboa, the Christmas fair in Parque Eduardo VII, runs from late November to early January with an ice rink, a Ferris wheel and food stalls, free to enter. The Rossio Christmas market sells crafts and ginjinha until 24 December. Fado houses in Alfama and Mouraria have shows every evening; book a table for weekends.

pages.title: Lisbon weather in November and December
pages.text: Lisbon in late November and December is mild: days around 15–17°C, nights around 9–11°C, with rain on roughly 8 to 10 days a month, often in short showers. Pack a light waterproof jacket and comfortable shoes for the hills; the cobbles get slippery when wet.

pages.title: Porto weather in December
pages.text: Porto is cooler and wetter than Lisbon in winter: December days reach about 14°C and nights drop to 6–7°C, with rain on around 12 days of the month. An umbrella and layers are essential; the riverside can be windy.

pages.title: Barcelona in November and December 2026
pages.text: The Fira de Santa Llúcia Christmas market fills the square in front of Barcelona Cathedral from 27 November to 23 December 2026, open about 10:00 to 21:00. The Christmas lights along Passeig de Gràcia switch on in late November. Camp Nou hosts FC Barcelona home matches most weekends; tickets sell online.

pages.title: Getting around Barcelona and from the airport
pages.text: The Aerobús runs from El Prat airport to Plaça de Catalunya every 5 to 10 minutes and takes about 35 minutes (EUR 7.25 one way). Metro line L9 Sud also reaches both terminals. A taxi to the centre costs about EUR 35–40. The Hola Barcelona travel card covers unlimited metro and bus rides for 2 to 5 days.

pages.title: Where to stay in Barcelona: neighbourhoods compared
pages.text: The Gothic Quarter is atmospheric and walkable but busy and noisy at night. Eixample has wide streets, Gaudí's Casa Batlló and La Pedrera, and quieter, larger hotels. El Born mixes boutique hotels, the Picasso Museum and good bars. Barceloneta is right on the beach, livelier in summer.

pages.title: Barcelona weather in late autumn and winter
pages.text: Barcelona stays mild in winter: November days around 17°C and December around 14°C, nights near 8–10°C. It is mostly sunny with a few rainy days. Too cold for swimming for most, fine for long walks along the seafront.

pages.title: Paris in November and December 2026
pages.text: The Champs-Élysées Christmas lights switch on in the last week of November 2026 and stay on until early January. Christmas markets run at the Tuileries Garden and at La Défense from late November to late December. Galeries Lafayette's window displays and Christmas tree draw crowds from mid-November.

pages.title: Paris airports to the city centre
pages.text: From Charles de Gaulle, RER B reaches Châtelet in about 35 minutes (EUR 13); flat-rate taxis cost EUR 56 to the Right Bank and EUR 65 to the Left Bank. From Orly, metro line 14 reaches the centre in about 25 minutes, and taxis cost EUR 36–44. Inside Paris, the metro is the quickest way around.

pages.title: Where to stay in Paris: the arrondissements compared
pages.text: Le Marais (3rd and 4th) has boutique hotels, galleries and falafel on Rue des Rosiers. Saint-Germain-des-Prés (6th) is classic Left Bank: cafés, bookshops and calm evenings. Montmartre is hilly and village-like with views from Sacré-Cœur, a bit further out. The Opéra and Louvre area suits first-timers and shoppers.

pages.title: Paris weather in November and December
pages.text: Paris is cool and often grey in late autumn: November days around 10–11°C, December around 7–8°C, nights near 3–5°C, with frequent light rain. Bring a warm coat, a scarf and an umbrella.

pages.title: Rome in November and December 2026
pages.text: The Christmas market in Piazza Navona runs from early December 2026 to 6 January. St Peter's Square gets its Christmas tree and nativity scene in early December, and Midnight Mass at the Vatican needs free tickets booked weeks ahead. Many museums open late on Fridays in December.

pages.title: Getting around Rome and from the airports
pages.text: The Leonardo Express train links Fiumicino airport with Termini in 32 minutes (EUR 14). Taxis from Fiumicino to the historic centre have a fixed fare of EUR 55; from Ciampino, EUR 40. The historic centre is best on foot; the metro skips much of it, and buses are slow in traffic.

pages.title: Where to stay in Rome
pages.text: The Centro Storico around the Pantheon and Piazza Navona puts most sights within a walk. Trastevere is charming and lively at night, with cobbled lanes and trattorias. Monti, near the Colosseum, has independent shops and wine bars. Termini is convenient for trains but less pleasant; Prati near the Vatican is calm and residential.

pages.title: Rome weather in November and December
pages.text: Rome stays fairly mild: November days around 17°C and December around 13°C, nights near 5–8°C. November is one of the wetter months, with rain on about 9 days. Fewer crowds make it a good time for the Vatican Museums and the Colosseum.

pages.title: London in November and December 2026
pages.text: Hyde Park Winter Wonderland opens on 20 November 2026 and runs until early January, with rides, an ice rink and food stalls; entry is free off-peak but must be booked. The Southbank Centre Winter Market runs along the Thames from mid-November. The Regent Street and Oxford Street lights go on in early November.

pages.title: London airports to the centre
pages.text: From Heathrow, the Elizabeth line reaches Paddington and Tottenham Court Road in about 30–40 minutes (around GBP 13); the Heathrow Express to Paddington takes 15 minutes. From Gatwick, the Gatwick Express runs to Victoria in 30 minutes. Contactless payment works on the Tube, buses and trains, with daily caps.

pages.title: Where to stay in London
pages.text: Covent Garden and Soho put theatres, restaurants and shopping on your doorstep but cost more. Shoreditch is creative and buzzy, with street art and nightlife. The South Bank has river walks, the Tate Modern and the London Eye. Kensington is elegant and close to the big museums; the City empties at weekends.

pages.title: London weather in November and December
pages.text: London in late autumn is mild but damp: November days around 11°C, December around 8°C, nights near 3–5°C, with light rain on about half the days. Daylight is short, with sunset around 16:00 in December.

pages.title: Amsterdam in November and December 2026
pages.text: The Amsterdam Light Festival lights the canals with art installations from late November 2026 to mid-January; canal boat tours run every evening and sell out at weekends. Sinterklaas arrives by boat in mid-November. Ice rinks open at the Museumplein in December.

pages.title: Getting around Amsterdam and from Schiphol
pages.text: Trains from Schiphol reach Amsterdam Centraal in about 15 minutes and run every few minutes (EUR 5.70). Inside the city, trams cover most areas and contactless cards work for check-in and check-out. Renting a bike is the local way around; watch for tram tracks.

pages.title: Where to stay in Amsterdam
pages.text: The canal ring in Centrum is postcard Amsterdam but busy, with small, pricey rooms. The Jordaan has quiet canals, cafés and independent shops. De Pijp, near the Albert Cuyp Market and Museumplein, is lively and more local, with plenty of restaurants.

pages.title: Amsterdam weather in November and December
pages.text: Amsterdam is cool, windy and often wet in winter: November days around 10°C, December around 7°C, nights near 2–4°C. Expect drizzle on many days and short daylight.

pages.title: Berlin in November and December 2026
pages.text: Berlin has more than 70 Christmas markets from late November 2026; the Gendarmenmarkt and Charlottenburg Palace markets are the most atmospheric, and the one at Gendarmenmarkt charges a small entry fee. The Festival of Lights is in October, so November is quieter until the markets open.

pages.title: Getting around Berlin and from BER airport
pages.text: From BER airport, the FEX express and regional trains reach Hauptbahnhof in about 30 minutes; an ABC ticket costs EUR 4.70. The U-Bahn and S-Bahn run late, and all night at weekends. A Berlin WelcomeCard bundles transport with museum discounts.

pages.title: Where to stay in Berlin
pages.text: Mitte is central, with Museum Island, the Brandenburg Gate and many large hotels. Kreuzberg is diverse and nightlife-heavy, with street food and canal-side bars. Prenzlauer Berg is leafy and family-friendly, with cafés and Sunday flea markets at Mauerpark.

pages.title: Berlin weather in November and December
pages.text: Berlin turns cold in late autumn: November days around 7°C, December around 4°C, nights near or below freezing. Snow is possible in December. Dress warmly for the Christmas markets.

pages.title: Prague in November and December 2026
pages.text: The Old Town Square and Wenceslas Square Christmas markets open on 28 November 2026 and run into early January, with a tree lighting on the first evening. Classical concerts fill churches across the Old Town most evenings in December.

pages.title: Getting around Prague and from the airport
pages.text: The Airport Express bus runs to the main railway station in about 35 minutes; bus 119 connects with metro line A at Nádraží Veleslavín. A 90-minute ticket costs CZK 46. Trams are the best way around the centre, and most sights are walkable.

pages.title: Where to stay in Prague
pages.text: The Old Town is the heart of Prague, near the Astronomical Clock and Charles Bridge, and busy day and night. Malá Strana below the castle is quieter and romantic. Vinohrady is residential and elegant, with good cafés and wine bars a short tram ride from the centre.

pages.title: Prague weather in November and December
pages.text: Prague is cold in winter: November days around 7°C, December around 3°C, nights below freezing at times. Snow is possible from December, which makes the Old Town look magical but the cobbles slippery.

pages.title: Tallinn in November and December 2026
pages.text: The Tallinn Christmas Market on Town Hall Square opens in late November 2026 and runs until early January, with a tall Christmas tree, handicrafts and mulled wine. Telliskivi Creative City holds design markets at weekends. Days are short, with sunset around 15:20 in December.

pages.title: Getting around Tallinn and from the airport
pages.text: Tallinn Airport is only 4 km from the centre: tram 4 reaches the city in about 20 minutes, and an ACME ride takes 10–15 minutes for around EUR 8–12. Ferries from Helsinki arrive at the Old City Harbour, a 10-minute walk from the Old Town. Public transport is free for registered residents; visitors pay EUR 2 per ride.

pages.title: Where to stay in Tallinn
pages.text: The Old Town is a UNESCO-listed medieval centre with cobbled lanes and boutique hotels. Kalamaja and Telliskivi have wooden houses, design shops and the best cafés. The Rotermann Quarter and the area around Viru keskus hold the big modern hotels, close to the harbour and the Old Town.

pages.title: Tallinn weather in November and December
pages.text: Tallinn is dark and cold in winter: November days around 3–4°C, December around 0°C, with frequent snow or sleet from December. Pack warm boots and a hat.
